output.name: Ketsa
output.myth: In the hungry winter the hearths ran low and the goats were brought in past the door-stones one by one. Ketsa, a grey nanny with a torn ear, would not come. She stood on the cliff edge with the salt wind in her coat and bleated at the byre until the men gave up calling. Tavo came up the cliff laughing and tried to push her off, and she held her feet and butted him back. Tavo cannot be bargained with, so he only laughed harder and went off down the wind. Then Hesk, who winds every string and keeps count of everything that stays out, came to the edge. She did not scold. She lifted the goat up to the north end of the Spindle, where nothing sets, and hung her there where she could see. Now every hearth-door on the islands can find her from the step. When the wind is wrong in the night, the old women say, she is looking for the door she left, and Hesk keeps her lamp lit so she will not be lost. Mend your nets, child, and do not stand so long on the edge.
output.verse:
Ketsa, the stubborn
Stood on the cliff in the wind
Hesk keeps her in sight

The foreleg star (45333) at about (382, 297) lands on the inner edge of the right leg, and the hind leg (48319) and hind hoof (47965) sit on the left leg outline, so the leg stars are roughly placed.

Draw the neck as a thicker curve from the head down to the chest star 45075 at about (380, 252) so the throat is visible. Remove or redraw the notch near (258-275, 237-250) as a beard or ear.
